banner.title: k8tz
banner.tagline: A mutating webhook that gives every pod the America/New_York timezone, so logs and cron schedules agree across the cluster.

art.about: a webhook that stamps a timezone onto every new pod
art.title: How k8tz sets the timezone

explainer.title: One webhook, one timezone, every namespace but its own

steps.title: Admit
steps.text: On each pod create, the webhook adds an init container that copies zone data and sets TZ, so processes run on New York time.
steps.scene: a webhook gate stamping a clock onto a new pod

steps.title: Exempt
steps.text: The webhook skips its own namespace, system-controller, by name, so the controller itself never runs through it.
steps.scene: a pod outside a fenced ring

steps.title: Schedule
steps.text: CronJobs get spec.timeZone, so a schedule written as 03:00 runs at 03:00 local time, not UTC.
steps.scene: a calendar with a local-time clock face

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Two replicas sit behind a PDB and a hostname spread. Every container has request equal to limit.

steps.title: Trust
steps.text: cert-manager issues the webhook serving certificate from a self-signed Issuer, so the API server can call it over TLS.
steps.scene: a seal on a certificate card

facts.label: failurePolicy: pod create blocks if down
